title: 18.125 Measure and Integration
authors: Ethan Brown (LaTeX lecture notes prepared from the instructor's handwritten notes)
description: Graduate first course on Lebesgue integration in 24 lectures with typed notes: σ-algebras and measurable functions; positive measures and the integral; monotone and dominated convergence; Lebesgue measure on R^n (construction, Carathéodory criterion, Cantor set, a non-measurable set, invariance); Riesz representation for positive linear functionals; Lusin and Egoroff; modes of convergence; Jensen, Hölder and Minkowski; L^p spaces and Riesz–Fischer; density theorems; Fubini and product measures; convolution and mollifiers; the maximal function and Lebesgue differentiation. Assignments are references to exercises in Rudin's Real and Complex Analysis.
rightsNotes: Content is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 by MIT OpenCourseWare (licence link on every course page; terms on the OCW terms-of-use page): attribution and share-alike required, commercial use excluded. Corniversity is private and non-commercial.

Importing the lecture-notes PDFs for personal study and citation is within the licence. The assignments are references to a commercial textbook (Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis) and are not copied; every Corniversity exercise is original or labelled adapted_with_attribution.
The lecture-notes page states that the notes were prepared in LaTeX by Ethan Brown, a former student in the class, using Professor Viaclovsky's handwritten notes.

syllabus: prerequisite 18.100 Analysis I; required text Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis (McGraw-Hill, 1986 ed.); recommended Jones, Lebesgue Integration on Euclidean Space, and Evans–Gariepy, Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions; grade from attendance and homework, no exams
calendar: 24 lectures with topic lists; homework 1 due at lecture 8, homework 2 at lecture 12, homework 3 at lecture 20
lecture notes page: 24 entries with topic lists, each linking a resource page whose PDF URL was recorded
assignments page: three homeworks referencing Rudin chapters 1–3 (no PDFs)
lecture PDFs 1–5: 3, 4, 3, 4 and 5 pages respectively, no printed page labels, dated 4, 9, 11, 16 and 18 September 2003 in the footer
limitations: Lecture PDFs 1–5 were downloaded and text-extracted on 2026-10-30; page indices in the pdf locators below refer to those files. Lecture PDFs 6–24 were not opened: their URLs were recorded from the OCW resource pages (opened), so those locators are file-level only.

The notes are a terse LaTeX transcription of handwritten lectures. Statement numbering restarts at 0.1 in every lecture, so a citation must name the lecture. Some statements carry slips (lecture 3, Theorem 0.2(1) reads 'E ⊂ R' where 'E ∈ M' is meant; lecture 2, Corollary 0.4(b) has 'min{f mg}' for 'min{f, g}'). Corniversity lessons restate every result with its hypotheses in full.
The assignments are exercise references into Rudin's book (commercial); they are not copied and are not used as Corniversity exercises.
The syllabus mentions the Radon–Nikodym theorem, Hausdorff measure and the area and coarea formulas; the published notes end at Marcinkiewicz interpolation (lecture 24) and do not cover them.
There are no lecture videos for this course.
